title: SecureResource
description: A protected object in an access control model — an API, database, file, service, UI area or stream — named as the target of authorization decisions and owning the set of ResourceOperations permitted on it and any FieldAccessControls over its fields. It is the 'object' of a subject-action-object triple, not the grant, rule or operation applied to it. Use InformationEntity instead when the thing protected is a logical information asset (e.g. customer PII) governed by InformationRight grants and classification, independent of the system resource that stores or exposes it. Use ResourceOperation instead when the element is a specific verb (read, approve, export) permitted on the resource rather than the resource itself. Use Permission instead when the element is a grant of an action on a resource assigned to a role, rather than the resource being protected. Use FieldAccessControl instead when the restriction applies to a single field's masking or redaction inside a resource rather than to the resource as a whole.

resource.description: Canonical identifier of the protected object as used in authorization checks — e.g. an API path pattern ('/api/orders/*'), table name, bucket URI or permission-string resource key; set it to the exact value enforcement code matches against.

type.description: Category of protected resource, used to apply appropriate access control and audit policies per NIST SP 800-53 AC-3.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what the resource contains or exposes and why it requires protection; set it when the identifier alone does not convey sensitivity or scope.

x-dr-standard: NIST SP 800-53 AC-3 (Access Enforcement) — protected object; XACML 3.0 Resource attribute category
x-dr-evidence: A route group, controller or API path prefix wrapped by an authorization guard or middleware (e.g. @PreAuthorize, router.use(requireAuth), [Authorize]) that names the protected resource

A resource identifier string used as the object argument in permission checks (e.g. can(user, 'update', 'invoice'), enforcer.enforce(sub, 'orders', act)) or as a resource entry in a Casbin/OPA/IAM policy file
A database table, bucket or topic declared in an IAM/RLS/ACL configuration (e.g. Postgres row-level security policy, S3 bucket policy, Kafka ACL) restricting which principals may operate on it
